projects.name: Meetly
projects.summary: A browser-based video meeting app for small groups: calls for up to six people, screen sharing, chat and five multiplayer games, with nothing to install.

story.challenge: Small groups end up juggling a call app, a chat and a separate game site, and most video tools ask people to install something first.
story.approach: I built Meetly on my own. Calls run peer to peer over WebRTC, with screen sharing, mute and camera indicators, and room chat that keeps history for late joiners. Bingo, Zero & Cross, a vanishing variant, Dots & Houses and Word Search run inside the meeting, and the server enforces the rules so cards stay private and moves can't be faked.
story.outcome: Live on Vercel with the backend on Render. It has accounts and meeting history, expiring sessions, password reset by email, invite links by URL or room code, and a pre-rendered landing page with structured data for search.

projects.name: Thandak
projects.summary: A free heat-safety service in Hindi and English that tells a family how risky today's heat is and what to do, on the web, Android, iOS and WhatsApp.

story.challenge: Heatwave warnings in India are generic. A family needs to know what today's heat means for each person at home, in their language, without installing anything.
story.approach: On a team of three, I built the backend in phases: alerts, per-person advice, saved homes, an assisted mode for ASHA and NGO workers, and calibration. I also added city heat-hotspot maps, a Delhi ward cooling scenario with a rupee budget planner, GeoJSON and printable ward exports, an outdoor-work card with hourly heat levels, and the signed Android release build.
story.outcome: Heat levels come only from the forecast and IMD's rules, every number in the advice is evidence-backed, and room temperature is estimated by an XGBoost model and always shown as a range.

projects.name: PaperSetu
projects.summary: An offline Android app for school teachers, in Hindi and English, that builds exam question papers in minutes and exports print-ready PDFs.

story.challenge: Teachers spend hours typing question papers by hand, fitting them to the school's format, and making separate sets so students can't copy from each other.
story.approach: I built PaperSetu on my own. A teacher picks the board, class, chapters and marks, chooses questions from the built-in bank, previews and edits the paper, then exports a PDF with up to three sets and an answer key, prints it or shares it on WhatsApp. The interface is HTML, CSS and JavaScript inside a Kotlin WebView, with native PDF and Word export.
story.outcome: Number templates give every set fresh values and work out the answer key automatically. Gemini drafts or rewords questions, approved ones join a shared bank, and school groups can see which questions colleagues have already used. Accounts sync through Firebase, and a Cloudflare Worker handles email and AI.

stats.label: sets per paper, plus an answer key

projects.name: PrepWise
projects.summary: Upload your resume and an AI voice agent interviews you for the role, then scores every answer and shows where you are weak.

story.challenge: Practising interviews alone is hard: reading questions off a list is nothing like answering a real person out loud, and nobody tells you what to fix.
story.approach: The app parses an uploaded resume (PDF or DOCX, via Mammoth) and Google Gemini writes role-specific questions in under two seconds. Vapi runs the live voice interview with speech-to-text, turn-taking and automatic transcripts. A Gemini evaluation step scores each answer on relevance, structure and completeness.
story.outcome: Firebase Auth and Firestore keep every interview, track weak areas across sessions, and power a performance dashboard for returning users. About ten beta users have tried it.

projects.name: RDIS LMS
projects.summary: A learning management system for courses, lessons and quizzes, with XP, badges, streaks and leaderboards to keep students coming back.

story.challenge: Course platforms rarely keep students coming back. Our team of six set out to build an LMS with gamification at its core.
story.approach: I worked on the API: the PostgreSQL schema, seed data and Express server setup, JWT authentication and protected routes, quiz and assessment APIs, the admin dashboard and course content, lesson content management, and the gamification engine.
story.outcome: The platform is deployed on Vercel, and the team tracks progress with weekly reports generated from the repository.
